summary: A status report from SRI's Augmentation Research Center and Network Information Center. Its conversion to a PDP-10 running TENEX was nearly done after some obscure bugs, including a noisy ground traced to bad memory data. Reliability was about one crash every day or two, and work turned to network software.

eli5.summary: A team says their new computer mostly works now. It had a sneaky electrical problem that made it forget things, but it is fixed and they will connect to the network next.

subtitle: SRI's Network Information Center reports on TENEX conversion and network connection plans

tldr.problem: SRI's ARC-NIC has converted to a new PDP-10 running TENEX but has encountered reliability problems and must prepare for network service.
tldr.mechanism: The system had obscure bugs traced to bad memory data caused by a noisy ground on the memory bus. After fixing this hardware issue, reliability improved to one crash every day or two. The team is now bringing up the NCP and Telnet, with staged rollout plans.
tldr.outcome: Initial network access is planned in stages, starting with a few West Coast sites in June, broader access in August, and full file transfer and deferred execution by September.

facts.label: Reliability after fix
facts.value: One crash every day or two

today: RFC 153 is a status report from May 1971 documenting SRI-ARC and the Network Information Center preparing to offer network services. The staged approach and focus on reliability established patterns for rolling out new network services. SRI-ARC became a key node in early ARPANET operations and information distribution.

sections.title: Hardware Conversion Completed
sections.content: The Augmentation Research Center and Network Information Center at SRI has completed conversion to a DEC PDP-10 running TENEX. The process revealed several obscure bugs. After investigation, a critical problem was traced to bad data being written to memory, which was caused by a noisy ground on a chip in the drum-disk memory bus access control. Once fixed, reliability improved significantly to about one crash every day or two. System attention has shifted to measurement, tuning, and bringing up network software.
sections.eli5: Our new computer had a hidden electrical problem that made it forget data. We found it and fixed it. Now we can focus on the network parts.

sections.title: Staged Network Rollout
sections.content: The RFC outlines three stages of network service. Stage 0 (June 18) offers experimental access to a limited number of West Coast sites, providing access to the TENEX Executive, NICTNLS (a typewriter interface), and an experimental NICDSS (dialog support system), with a maximum of two simultaneous network users and a training course June 16-17. Stage 1 (August 2) expands to any network site with proper software, adds online access to documents, and supports 4-8 simultaneous users. Stage 2 (September 6) adds message delivery to remote sites, deferred execution for file preparation, and improved query facilities.
sections.eli5: We will roll out network service in three stages: first to a few nearby sites, then to anyone, then with full features like file transfer.

sections.title: Other Operations
sections.content: Offline, SRI handles RFC distribution and mailing to liaison people and station agents. The Network Information Center emphasizes the importance of unique document numbering for citation and cataloging. The RFC also includes recommendations on site documentation and notes work on maintaining an up-to-date catalog. The NIC invites feedback from liaison people and station agents on service improvements.
sections.eli5: We mail RFC's and documents to the network community. We also keep a catalog of everything and help coordinate information sharing.
